summary: Observations of a stationary orange object in the overcast sky to the Southeast then rapid departure: astronomical mistake with the rising sun.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification within an investigation report. This observation, previously classified as D and named SOLIGNAC (87) 1979, is one of a group of cases recently re-examined. On December 20, 1979, at approximately 8:45 a.m., three people observed a luminous and stationary phenomenon in the sky to the southeast for 30 to 40 seconds. The UAP is described as a very bright, reddish-orange mass, rectangular, oval, or circular in shape, depending on the witness account. Witnesses reported overcast, gray weather with a low cloud ceiling. The UAP suddenly rotated, taking on a cigar shape, and departed, leaving behind an orange trail that turned white. The object disappeared into the clouds. Descriptive details are provided in relation to the sun: "The object reminded me of a sunset," "The object in question was larger than the sun," "I thought it was an eclipse" (see investigation notes). The rising sun was precisely in the direction of observation, and its low angular altitude would explain the dominant color of the UAP, namely bright red. The variable shape of the UAP, the short duration of the observation, and its rapid departure are explained by the presence of clouds that obscured the Sun, visible only through a break in the cloud cover. This aspect of the phenomenon is supported by eyewitness accounts suggesting a UAP in a sky with uneven cloud cover. The object was partially and intermittently obscured by a dark cloud; the craft appeared to be propelled, then disappeared into the clouds. The presence of an uneven cloudy sky, the perfect consistency between the Sun's actual position and the location and description of the UAP, and the absence of any other solar sightings compared to the UAP sightings, all contribute to a case that leaves no doubt about the misinterpretation. This case is quite substantial (three witnesses gave their statements to the police), and the description of the observed UAP is fairly precise. Mistaking the sunrise for sunset is not uncommon in GEIPAN's records and affects all types of witnesses. GEIPAN classifies this case as A: Sunrise.

summary: Observations by a family for 15 minutes of 3 luminous discs flashing in the night sky: lack of information.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case, previously classified as D and named HERSERANGE (54) 1979, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On December 18, 1979, starting at 2:14 a.m., five members of the same family observed three luminous discs (the color varied from white to reddish-orange, according to witnesses) directly above a school for 15 minutes. They turn on and off. For some witnesses, these discs have an upward movement. This observation is characterized, on the one hand, by a strangeness perceived by the witnesses, apparently quite strong, judging by the repeated use of the terms UFO and saucer, and on the other hand, by the extreme paucity of the testimonies. It consists of three luminous discs that turn on and off (in a direction passing vertically through the school). This is the essential information (which fits almost in a single sentence) and common (the sentence is practically repeated) to the five statements from the same family: the parents and their three children, aged 10 to 13. The few additional details vary depending on the witness. The father and mother (T1 and T2) indicate (or have the impression, in T2's case) that the discs were rising in the sky. Two children, T3 and T5, provided no details about the movement, while T4 also didn't mention any vertical movement but was the only one to have seen one of the discs separate from the others. The color of the discs also varied between witnesses, being orange, white, or indistinct. Nothing is known about the position in the sky, the angular size, the orientation of the discs, or the type of sharp or precise outline of these lights (which would be an indication of their materiality), etc. With so little information, it is impossible to find an explanation. One might regret that the Gendarmerie or GEIPAN did not conduct further questioning or reconstructions; it is unrealistic to expect to do so 40 years later. On the other hand, this observation is characterized by a lack of intrinsic consistency, which discouraged further investigation. Indeed, when the strangeness is strong, testimonies are rarely brief, and even less so duplicated. The most unusual aspect here, compared to the mass of GEIPAN testimonies, is the lack of information regarding the circumstances of the UFO disappearances. The mother and three children went back to sleep while the UFOs were still there! All of this casts doubt on the reality of the perceived strangeness. It is also noted that T1 (the father) had previously made numerous sightings of flying saucers. These sightings and their repetition may have generated a strong emotional charge in him, which could explain why he insisted on waking the other witnesses, including the young children, by shouting "Flying saucers!" These other witnesses may therefore have been more impressed (even if it wasn't the first time) by T1's feelings than by the sighting itself, to the point of sharing in his experience. This would explain the repetition of minimal descriptions and why everyone went to bed, leaving the father alone with the sighting. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: lack of reliable information.

summary: Observation of a cigar-shaped, phosphorescent object.
description: On December 15, 1979, at approximately 2:00 AM, a witness observed a phosphorescent orange object in the sky from the third floor of their apartment. The object was cigar-shaped, vertical, and moved silently from north to south. It then disappeared into the urban landscape. No further accounts of this unexplained phenomenon were ever collected.

summary: Observation of 6 oval-shaped objects moving at high speed
description: On December 14, 1979, at approximately 9:30 PM, a young motorcyclist spotted six bright, oval-shaped objects in the sky. They moved rapidly in a formation of three and disappeared in a westward direction. No trace of the object or any other eyewitness accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of a saucer-shaped object moving at very high speed
description: On December 12, 1979, a night watchman observed a flying saucer-shaped object in the sky, slightly domed in the middle and tapering towards the edges. The object was orange. A purple and orange trail was visible behind it. It disappeared abruptly and at very high speed over the horizon. No other accounts of this phenomenon were collected, and information about it remains scarce.

summary: Observation of an object 4 to 5 meters high, oscillating. No noise. Upward trajectory.
description: On December 8, 1979, at 9:52 a.m., two witnesses from their homes spotted a crescent-shaped object, navy blue and white with no shine. It measured 4 to 5 meters in height. No unusual noise or light was observed. The object, close to the ground, swayed near a thicket. The observation lasted one minute and thirty seconds at a distance of 200 meters from the object. It disappeared, flying rapidly northward. Neither the witnesses nor the police found any trace of it on the ground.

summary: Observations by motor vehicles of a luminous object in the direction of the East: astronomical observations of the Moon.
description: This case of observation was recently re-examined (see the Investigation Notes document). On December 7, 1979, at approximately 9:15 PM, several motorists in the same geographical area spotted a luminous phenomenon in the sky that intrigued them. It appeared to be moving at low altitude and was seen in different forms depending on the witness (ball, parachute, capital L). The investigation did not yield any further information, apart from barking dogs heard from a nearby farm. This case is consistent (several independent witnesses), and the description of the observed UFO is precise. The sincerity and credibility of the witnesses have never been questioned. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, color) with a well-known astronomical object: the Moon at sunrise. Furthermore, the Moon was indeed visible in the area of the sky observed. It is not the visual perception of the witnesses that is the issue, but rather their interpretation of their observations based on their own experience (fatigue, night driving). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of weak strangeness is classified as A e, observations linked to a misidentification of the Moon.

summary: Observation of unusual lights.
description: On December 6, 1979, between 9:15 and 9:30 PM, several people observed intriguing luminous phenomena in the sky. A white luminous mass appeared to move from west to east, followed by the appearance of five orange luminous sources of varying shapes, described by different witnesses (lines or ovals). These lights gradually disappeared eastward, fading away. No other accounts of this phenomenon have been collected, leaving us with little information.

summary: observation of the movement of a ball with orange reflections.
description: On December 5, 1979, at approximately 5:40 PM, a witness observed a ball the size of an orange with an orange sheen. It moved by rotating on its axis and alternately rising and falling. No sound was heard. The observation lasted fifteen minutes before the ball disappeared in a very rapid southeasterly direction. The following day at the same time, the ball was visible again, but it changed size three times and disappeared to the west. Only one other witness had seen a similar phenomenon a few months earlier.

summary: Observation of a triangular object changing speed and direction
description: On December 3, 1979, at approximately 4:50 PM, two witnesses observed a triangular-shaped object emitting two trails of red smoke. As it passed over a radio tower, the object paused for a few seconds before moving on. The witnesses followed it visually until it was out of sight, the red smoke remaining visible until the end of the observation. A third witness observed a very bright point at the same time, but it was not possible to establish a correlation between the two sightings. The investigation failed to identify any air traffic corresponding to the observations, and the phenomenon remains unexplained.

summary: Observation of 8 aircraft-sized objects emitting a whistling sound
description: On December 2, 1979, at approximately 6:30 PM, a couple observed eight aircraft-sized objects emitting a whistling sound. These objects also emitted flashing red, green, blue, and yellow lights. They moved slowly, and the observation lasted about 20 minutes. The investigation failed to identify the cause of these phenomena.

summary: Observation by a motorist of a luminous ball following him during his journey on a winding road; sudden disappearance: perceptual illusion caused by the sudden observation of the Moon.
description: On December 1, 1979, at approximately 7:35 PM, a butcher was returning from his day at the market in Braux (04). He was driving his van on a winding section of the D110 when he suddenly saw a large, very bright sphere appear on his left. Its color changed from white to red, then from orange to yellow. The sphere emitted a high-pitched, beeping sound. The witness, very frightened, accelerated but noticed that the phenomenon followed him for about 2 km while the vehicle was traveling at approximately 70-80 km/h. After about 2 km, the phenomenon abruptly disappeared. No other witness statements were collected by the police. This case was initially classified as "unexplained observation, case D." It is one of the French cases that received media attention at the time (search for UFOs in Annot). The present conclusion results from a new investigation, made possible on the one hand by today's digital tools and on the other hand by an on-site reconstruction on a date within the Saros cycle, that is to say, on a date when the Moon, the Sun, and the Earth are in the exact same position as on the day of the observation (see the investigation report). The witness, having reported the presence of the full Moon at the start of his journey, paradoxically made no further mention of it, even though at several points along the route it should have appeared very bright precisely in the direction of observation of the presumed UFO. The elements glimpsed in the preliminary analysis phase (distance measurement with digital tools) were largely confirmed by an on-site reconstruction conducted under optimal conditions of similarity (Saros cycle and similar weather): the witness was found to have been the victim of a perceptual illusion caused by the sudden sighting of the Moon. In particular, it turns out that each location where moon observation was possible corresponds precisely to one of the locations where the witness described to the police the phenomenon he believed he had encountered. In fact, the presumed trajectory of the unidentified flying object (UFO), as imagined by the frightened witness, perfectly matches the apparent trajectory of the moon in relation to the curves of the road. The sudden appearance and disappearance of the phenomenon are also consistent with the moon's visibility to the driver of a vehicle traveling on that road that day. The element of surprise is heightened by a highly charged media context: the Cergy-Pontoise (95) UFO case is in full swing, and the young man allegedly abducted by the UFO has not yet reappeared. These elements likely induced a strong sense of fear in the witness who, placed in difficult observation conditions and an unsettling context (he was alone and far from any habitation), was unable to calmly analyze the situation he was suddenly confronted with. His descriptions of the phenomenon are classic and perfectly comparable to those commonly gathered in similar cases of mistaken identity with the Moon (a very frequent occurrence). The only unusual features that might have somewhat contradicted this well-known scenario are, firstly, the noise allegedly perceived during the observation and, secondly, the physiological repercussions suffered in the following days (intestinal obstruction). However, no evidence can be presented to support the objective reality of the first. Regarding the second, it likely appears to be a consequence of the stress caused by the observation on a pre-existing physiological condition (two similar previous episodes). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: Moon sighting.

summary: Observation of an electric arc on an overhead power line.
description: On November 29, 1979, at approximately 5:30 a.m., a witness observed a flashing blue light resembling an ambulance's flashing beacon. The gendarmerie investigation confirmed the phenomenon on site, which was clearly identified as an electrical arc between two wires of a power line.

summary: Observation of a bright point
description: On November 27, 1979, at approximately 4:15 PM, a witness observed a bright point of light passing across the sky for about two minutes. No further information is available.

summary: "The abduction" of Cergy-Pontoise.
description: The names of the various protagonists have been anonymized, as in the official reports. The story that follows received significant media attention due to the fact that the main protagonists never sought discretion; quite the opposite. The various events that comprise it took place over a relatively long period of time and in quite diverse locations. The amount of information is therefore substantial and was, among other things, the subject of technical note Ne6 GEPAN, referenced in the case documents. On November 26, 1979, around 5:00 a.m., the local police station received a phone call from T3 informing them that his "friend had been abducted by a UFO." A patrol was immediately dispatched to the scene. Seven police officers and gendarmes soon arrived at the location with three witnesses: T3, T2, and T1, friends of the missing man and witnesses to the "abduction." The witnesses explained that they were preparing to go sell jeans at the nearby market when they noticed a glow above the road. T1, who was driving the car, headed towards the glow. It then positioned itself above the car, enveloping it in fog and small, flashing orbs. When the fog dissipated, the glow disappeared "like a flash" into the sky. It was then that T3 realized that T1 was no longer in the car. When questioned by the authorities, the three witnesses displayed very different attitudes, ranging from indifference to extreme excitement. From the initial interviews, discrepancies emerged in their testimonies, and the reconstructions carried out also led to contradictions regarding the witnesses' schedules the day before and the morning of the disappearance, the car's position at the time of the incident, and the glow's trajectory. The gendarmerie alerted GEPAN on the 26th, but the press was also notified by one of the witnesses, and by the 27th, journalists and private investigators were flocking from all over the region. From the 28th, radio stations and newspapers were reporting the case in detail, with opinions and interpretations multiplying in response to various interviews. However, no new information emerged before December 3, 1979, when T1's mother informed the gendarmerie of her son's return, and T3 informed a radio station about his friend's return. The gendarmes indeed found T1 at T2's house, accompanied by his family and a journalist. T1 stated that he had found himself in a cabbage field near T2's building. GEPAN would try to gather as much objective information as possible on this widely publicized case. It will be extremely difficult for him to do so, as witnesses constantly evade the question of providing concrete evidence, preferring the company of journalists and certain private investigators with whom they were much more forthcoming. As press conferences and statements continue, the witnesses' accounts change, and it quickly becomes clear to the GEPAN investigators that the reported facts are not credible. This hypothesis is reinforced by a blood analysis showing that it is unlikely that "disappeared T1" experienced weightlessness. The discovery of a row of cabbages dried "by the luminous sphere" in the field where T1 reappeared will reignite the excitement in this small town. The investigation quickly revealed that these cabbages were perfectly normal and had been abandoned by their owner to be used as fertilizer, a fact confirmed by analysis of samples taken by GEPAN. Although the witnesses have consistently maintained their testimonies, including before the public prosecutor, GEPAN considers this a hoax whose unfolding discredits the scientific work it is trying to promote.

summary: Observation of a light source. No noise.
description: On November 26th, around 6:00 AM, a farmer in a field spotted a very bright white light source about seven or eight hundred meters away. This light had a slight vertical movement at an altitude of five or six meters. A dark, spherical area was seen beneath this light. The on-site investigation revealed no traces on the ground. No military training flights were recorded at that time on the day of the observation. No other witness statements were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information. The photographs taken by the gendarmes were not found in the gendarmerie file.

summary: Observation of rapidly moving luminous phenomena.
description: On November 25, 1979, at approximately 12:45 a.m., a witness in his garden observed a peculiar luminous phenomenon in the sky. He saw two pale green luminous trails moving parallel to each other in a northwest-southeast direction. These trails were preceded by objects moving very rapidly without any audible noise. Despite the presence of many people due to a local festival, no other witness statements or information were gathered about this phenomenon, for which we lack details.

summary: Observation of a diamond-shaped object. Abnormal behavior in sheep.
description: On November 21, 1979, a witness spotted an object about 100 meters away, equipped with several lights: three red and one orange, forming a diamond shape inscribed on a vertical plane. The orange light alternately replaced the red lights by rotating clockwise. Motionless and silent, the object hovered in the air. No unusual odor emanated from the craft, which then disappeared to the north, leaving a trail of whitish smoke. Sheep penned 600 meters away displayed great distress. A second witness reported seeing red lights forming a diamond shape. No traces were found on the ground, and no further information was gathered about this phenomenon, which remains unexplained.

summary: Observation of a fluorescent object. Buzzing sound
description: On November 18, 1979, at 3:20 a.m., a witness observed a circular, fluorescent object from their home. Flanked by two tail-like appendages of a gray-beige color, the object moved at low altitude and speed in a straight line from northwest to southeast. No sound was heard during the observation, which lasted only a few seconds. No other reports were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous triangular object.
description: On November 15, 1979, at approximately 7:30 a.m., a witness and his wife observed a white, triangular object from their home. This luminous object initially remained stationary, then moved very slowly southwest while rising. It gradually disappeared into the air. No other accounts of this phenomenon have been collected, and information about it remains scarce.

summary: Observation of red-orange luminous phenomena.
description: On November 14, 1979, at approximately 5:42 PM, an off-duty Air Force officer observed unusual luminous phenomena in the sky. Driving by car, the witness and his passenger suddenly saw two bright, reddish-orange lights. Quite close together, they stabilized at an altitude of about 100 meters above the woods and then disappeared one after the other. No noise was heard. Thirty seconds later, a nearly simultaneous double sonic boom occurred. The witness believed it was likely a high-altitude patrol breaking the sound barrier. One minute later, two more lights appeared at the same altitude and distance, but further north than the first two. Five seconds later, these lights disappeared one after the other. The local press also reported that several people in the area witnessed this phenomenon. No further testimony or details will be gathered by the gendarmerie on this phenomenon which remains unexplained.

summary: Observations of the movement of flying objects with a deme and flashing colored lights: lack of information.
description: On December 1, 1979, the gendarmerie learned through the press that residents of the same town had seen "crafts" or "objects" moving above Mareau-aux-Bois (45) on November 11, 1979, around 6:45 p.m. These objects were described as having a round shape, with a dome on top and flashing colored lights. The testimonies were brief but numerous (8 witnesses). The gendarmerie found a ninth witness who reported an observation made on November 25, 1979, at 9:30 p.m. above Courcy-aux-Loges (45). Due to the time elapsed between the events and their disclosure, the gendarmerie was unable to conduct any investigation. No further information has been gathered on this phenomenon, for which we lack data.

summary: Observation of a red luminous phenomenon.
description: On November 1, 1979, at approximately 6:15 PM, several witnesses observed a red luminous phenomenon in the sky. According to the witnesses, it consisted of one or two red spheres moving silently across the sky. This object followed a southwest-northeast trajectory. One of the witnesses reported seeing a trail of fire behind the object. No further information was gathered about this phenomenon, for which we lack data.

summary: Observations of a red phosphorescent object above a wood which rises while changing shape before disappearing: mistaken for the rising sun in an overcast sky.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. Its publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to ensure more relevant conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience acquired over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification within an investigation report. This case, previously classified as D and named THIVARS (28) 25.10.1979, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On October 25, 1979, at approximately 7:30 a.m., a driver and her two passengers were traveling on the D137 towards Chartres. Near the entrance to the village of Fresnay-le-Comte, they spotted a luminous object above a wooded area, which intrigued them. This object was a non-dazzling, rather phosphorescent red (T2). According to witnesses, it was shaped like an isosceles trapezoid (T1) or a bowl (T2). No unusual noise was heard during the observation, which lasted 15 to 20 seconds. The object rose, changing shape (rectangular then a simple line) before disappearing completely. Two witness statements were filed with the police. The details provided by witnesses suggest a possible misidentification of the sun as rising, given that the UFO is described as phosphorescent and compared to a sunset: "like when the sun is very red in the evening at (T2)," and "this shape had the color of the sun when it is red and not dazzling, like when it will rain the next day at (T1)." It has been verified that the sun was perfectly aligned with the observation point and was rising. The confirmed presence of cloud cover very likely prevented the witnesses from identifying the sun. This same cloud cover, with the probable presence of small breaks or clearings, all in motion due to the prevailing wind (greater than 15 km/h), can also perfectly explain the evolution of the UFO's shape as well as its disappearance, the sun gradually disappearing behind a cloud. It should also be noted that the UFO emitted a light that illuminated the woods, which is consistent with the sun. The witnesses never mentioned seeing the sun, even though it was rising on the horizon, precisely in the direction they indicated. The perfect consistency between the sun's true position and the location and description of the UFO leaves no doubt about the misinterpretation. It is not the witnesses' visual perception that is at fault, but their interpretation of their observation based on their feelings (driving, surprise, poor weather conditions). Consequently, this case of weak strangeness is classified by GEIPAN as UFO A: observation linked to a misinterpretation of the rising sun.

summary: Observation of a flying object in the shape of an airship.
description: On October 10, 1979, at approximately 7:55 a.m., a witness observed an unusual object in the sky. Shaped like a dirigible, this object moved at a constant speed along a horizontal trajectory toward the northwest. No sound from the object was heard during the entire observation. The object gradually disappeared into the sky. No other reports were collected about this object, which resembled a dirigible or the Super Guppy (a cargo plane replaced in 1996 by the Beluga), but about which we lack information.

summary: Probable sighting of an aircraft.
description: On October 9, 1979, at approximately 11:30 PM, several people spotted a luminous flying object at low altitude. It moved while making an impressive noise, which frightened some witnesses and animals. These people likely witnessed the passage of an aircraft, a theory confirmed by one of the witnesses who recognized the taillights of a helicopter.

summary: Observation of a high-altitude object
description: On September 24, 1979, at 7:42 a.m., a witness first saw a trail in the sky, which he mistook for that of a jet engine. He then noticed an object that remained stationary for 10 to 15 seconds. Orange in color, it was disc-shaped. Suddenly, the object moved at very high speed and turned a brilliant white before disappearing. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of a luminous object. Sudden disappearance.
description: On September 23, 1979, around 6:00 AM, several people observed a luminous point in the sky moving silently in a northeast direction. This point emitted green and red colors. Moments later, the witnesses' car was flooded with light that covered the entire road. Suddenly, the light went out, and one of the witnesses saw a shape rise to an altitude of 45 degrees, without any sound, but leaving behind a red flame. The investigation at the scene revealed no clues, and no further information was gathered about this phenomenon, which remains unexplained.

summary: Observation of a luminous disk 4 meters in diameter.
description: On September 20, 1979, around 11:00 PM, several people observed a bright red object moving rapidly across the sky from west to east. A circle approximately 4 meters in diameter was crossed by two red diagonals. It flashed and made a loud noise. The object, which had turned white, disappeared behind the hills. No further accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of a red glow with a rapid approach towards the witnesses.
description: On September 19, 1979, at 10:00 PM, two witnesses, while jogging, observed a red, ball-shaped glow in the sky that shimmered like a star. Suddenly, this glow moved at a dizzying speed, approaching the witnesses. No noise, movement of air, or heat was observed. Tracing a curve, the glow stopped for three to four seconds approximately 200 meters above the edge of the forest. A dark mass appeared within the glow. The phenomenon then vanished abruptly. No further witness accounts or information were gathered regarding this unexplained event.

summary: Observation of a bright white object. Rapid movement.
description: On September 17, 1979, at approximately 7:45 a.m., a person noticed a fixed point of light in the sky. White and oval in shape, this single point then quickly and horizontally crossed the area where three airplanes were flying. The object disappeared to the east. Following an appeal for witnesses published in the local press, several people contacted the authorities. They reported seeing a peculiar object in the sky that same day, but over a longer period. However, the varying descriptions did not allow for precise identification of the object.

summary: Observation of an oval object rising towards the sky. Sudden disappearance.
description: On September 7, 1979, at approximately 4:30 a.m., two witnesses observed, for less than five seconds, an oval-shaped green object with four white lights, surrounded by a black circle. The colors were very vivid and phosphorescent. This object ascended rapidly in the sky at a 45° angle, following a south-north direction. It then suddenly disappeared. No other accounts have been collected regarding this phenomenon, for which we lack information.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry.
description: On September 8, 1979, at approximately 4:30 a.m., two witnesses observed a circular object passing across the sky from their bedroom. It moved at high speed while losing altitude. An orange halo of light surrounded the object. Attempting to open the window, one of the witnesses received an electric shock. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected, and the EDF (French electricity company) station detected no anomalies on its power lines. These individuals likely witnessed an atmospheric reentry. The electric shock experienced by one of the witnesses, even though it occurred at the time of the observation, cannot be directly linked to the type of phenomenon observed.

summary: Luminous spherical object making a U-turn
description: In September 1979, at approximately 6:30 PM, a witness, while alone outside his property, observed a luminous object appearing on the horizon. This object moved very slowly in a south-north direction. Thinking it was a passenger plane, the witness kept his eyes fixed on it. The plane stopped above him: the witness then observed a very bright, spherical object, metallic gray in color. After stopping for about a minute, the object moved off again in the opposite direction, reached the horizon in a few seconds, and disappeared completely. No unusual noise was heard during the observation. This very late (October 2007) and poorly documented testimony does not allow for a serious investigation that could validate or refute certain hypotheses, such as a passenger plane in a turn, a balloon subjected to wind shear, etc.

summary: Observation of bright points of various colours in the sky.
description: During the month of September and until October 4, 1979, a witness and his wife observed intriguing luminous points in the sky. These points were visible in clear weather between 7:00 PM and 11:30 PM. They were red, green, and white and flashed. Together, these points formed a sphere. The gendarmes, during various night shifts, saw no similar occurrences. No other witness statements were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of several lights in the sky.
description: On August 31, 1978, several people observed three lights in the sky around 9:15 PM. An initial orange light was observed for about fifteen minutes. Subsequently, two other silver lights appeared and moved rapidly before disappearing instantly. The witnesses decided to move outside the city and saw the lights reappear around 11:00 PM. They observed them for an hour with binoculars. The phenomenon disappeared completely around 12:15 AM. No further reports were recorded concerning this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of a ring of mushrooms 11 meters in diameter on the ground.
description: On August 30, 1979, a farmer went to a rye field and noticed a spherical circle 10.5 meters in diameter. He observed that the grass was greener inside the circle than in the surrounding meadow. Around September 20, this same witness discovered that mushrooms of the "rose-like" type had grown both inside and outside the circle. This phenomenon had already been observed in meadows in the area.

summary: Observation of a very bright, rectangular-shaped object the size of an airplane.
description: On August 28, 1979, at 8:45 PM, a witness observed a passenger plane flying overhead through binoculars. He then saw a very bright, rectangular shape behind and above the aircraft. No further information about this phenomenon was provided by the gendarmerie brigades near Orly Airport or by the head of the Orly South regional control center.

summary: Observation of an aluminum-colored craft silently spinning like a top and flying over the streetlights of an urban area: lack of reliable information.
description: Recent testimony (October 20, 2012) of an old observation. A witness reports having observed, around midnight on August 24, 1979, a silver-colored object that was stationary but silently rotating above power lines in an urban area. No other testimonies have been collected regarding this phenomenon. A detailed analysis of the testimony by a university psychologist reveals several inconsistencies and does not allow for the conclusion that the reported events were entirely experienced, but rather that it is more likely a mixture of real events and imagined elements or elements from other accounts. Memory may have confused these elements after more than 30 years. It should also be noted that adolescence is a period conducive to the creation of "false memories." An investigation 30 years later would not yield reliable information. This case is classified as "C" due to a lack of reliable information, cross-checking, or other factors.

summary: Likely sighting of an airplane illuminated by the sun
description: On August 22, 1979, at approximately 10:45 PM, two witnesses observed a bright point of light that intrigued them. Initially stationary between 100 and 150 meters above the golf course, it then moved westward, decreasing in intensity. The witness later observed the point with binoculars and reported seeing two yellow parallelograms. No other accounts of this phenomenon were collected. The various shapes observed could be due to binocular aberrations, common when using low-quality binoculars to observe a point of light. It is likely that the observed phenomenon was an airplane illuminated by the sun.

summary: Observation of 3 luminous discs.
description: On August 11, 1979, at approximately 9:10 PM, several people observed a peculiar luminous phenomenon. As the sun set, three reddish-orange rings were visible on the horizon below a cloud cover. These discs then dissipated, taking the form of a horizontal line that quickly disappeared northward into the clouds. No other reports were collected in the area. Based on the witnesses' descriptions, it is likely that this phenomenon was an optical illusion caused by the setting sun reflecting off a low cloud cover.

summary: Observation of 3 balls of different sizes.
description: On August 5, 1979, between 11:00 PM and 11:30 PM, a witness and some police officers observed unusual luminous phenomena in the sky. Orbs of varying sizes and colors shone to the left of the moon. Some moved jerkily from left to right, sometimes at very high speeds. They disappeared into the clouds. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of a slowly moving ball. No noise.
description: On the night of July 27-28, 1979, around midnight, a person was awakened by a strange light in their bedroom. The witness then observed a white, luminous sphere through the window. It moved very slowly from northwest to northeast without making any noise. This sphere was larger than the moon. It disappeared, hidden by the buildings. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of a bright orange point with a trail.
description: On July 25, 1979, at approximately 9:30 PM, two witnesses observed a bright orange point in the sky that moved and then appeared to stop. The brightness of this small point suddenly decreased sharply. It disappeared instantly, leaving only a white trail. No other accounts of this phenomenon were collected, and we lack information about it.

summary: Observation of a cigar-shaped object rotating on itself.
description: On July 23, 1979, at approximately 9:40 PM, a driver and her passengers observed a peculiar object for several minutes, which intrigued them. This luminous, orange, cigar-shaped object, two meters long, moved rapidly from southeast to northwest. Flying at an altitude of 200 meters, it appeared to rotate. It quickly disappeared over the horizon. No other accounts of this phenomenon were collected, for which we lack data.

summary: Observations by two distinct groups of witnesses of a stationary luminous phenomenon of yellow-orange colour projecting a blue beam rotating regularly through 360°: strange phenomenon of medium or strong consistency.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case study, previously classified as D and named LES OLLIERES (07) 1979, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On July 21, 1979, a first group of people (T1 and his wife) observed, from 10:45 PM to 11:28 PM, a stationary, colored luminous phenomenon at the summit of a ridge in the direction of the "Serre de Pieroulet." The UFO was described as a "lighthouse" with a powerful yellow-orange light source projecting a blue beam that rotated regularly through 360 degrees and swept across the ground. During the 45-minute observation, no unusual noises were heard. T1 was about to take a photograph when the UFO suddenly went dark. The next day, these first witnesses learned that their closest neighbors (T2 and his wife), upon closing their shutters around 11:00 PM, had noticed a luminous UFO in the same direction. T2 and his wife observed the UFO for about ten minutes before going to bed. The Gendarmerie was notified the following day by T1. Only T1 and T2 gave statements. The UFO was particularly well described by the main witness, T1. His report allowed us to realize that the UFO's appearance and behavior were very unusual and did not correspond to any known phenomenon, whether natural or artificial (see the investigation report). Indeed, the only possible explanation could be a helicopter (since the UFO was indeed stationary in the sky) using a searchlight, but whose beam, inexplicably, was blue, a different color from the source, and rotated continuously without any apparent purpose of surveillance or illumination. As witness T1 had unfortunately passed away, it was impossible for us to continue the investigation further, which could have included, for example, a cognitive interview or an on-site reconstruction. The three other witnesses could not be located, but it is also possible, almost 40 years after the events, that they too have died. T1's scientific expertise closely relates to everything concerning light and color, as well as their impact on their environment. It so happens that his observation concerns precisely luminous and colored phenomena falling exactly within his area of expertise. This coincidence reinforces the already established factual basis, given the precision and completeness of the description: - the witness uses descriptive parameters that he understands; - in terms of reliability, the widespread recognition that witness T1 already enjoyed makes it unlikely that he would want to add any particular element of strangeness to an observation in order to gain recognition. On the contrary, the attitude of recognized scientists generally leads to maintaining the greatest possible distance from UFOs. In this context, the testimony is representative of a genuinely strange experience and a matter of knowledge for this scientist. T1 did not take any photographs. He presumably owns a camera, but it is understood that the witness retrieved his equipment at the moment the UFO disappeared. We can regret the mediocre quality of T2's testimony, which is not very detailed, and the absence of the two other testimonies, those of the wives. Nevertheless, T2's testimony, besides placing the UFO in the same direction and at the same time, confirms T1's testimony on the points that constitute the essence of the strangeness: a fixed yellow/orange glow, and a blue light sweeping across the ground. T2 does not mention the beam, and the strangeness experienced seems weak (the witnesses stopped observing and went to bed). In the current GEIPAN methodology, the present level of strangeness and consistency necessitates conducting a field investigation with the witness for reconstruction and a cognitive interview. This latter process is likely to positively or negatively impact the assessment of both strangeness and consistency. However, it is not possible for a case revisited so long afterward. Therefore, the evaluation of the present case is carried out according to the current criteria for considering strangeness and consistency (see GEIPAN news article GEIPAN's classification methodology) as if the field investigation had been conducted and had been completely neutral (no additional or additional information), which is sometimes the case. However, to highlight this methodological difference, the classification is based on ABCD and not on the current ABC D1/D2 classification, which, for unexplained cases, corresponds to a stronger validation of the unexplained nature of the phenomenon. Here, the case is on the borderline between an unexplained case and one that cannot be investigated due to a lack of consistency in the case file, resulting from the absence of an on-site GEIPAN investigation. Consequently, the case is classified as D: Strange phenomenon of medium or strong consistency.

summary: Observation of a round object, slowly descending and rising.
description: On July 20, 1979, around 10:00 AM, several people observed a peculiar bright shape in the sky for about twenty minutes. Depending on the location of the witnesses, this ovoid object measured between 80 cm and 5 m in diameter and appeared metallic or black. It initially hovered above a house, then rose and gradually moved away without making any noise. According to the gendarmerie, no unusual sightings were reported from airfields or bases in the region, and no advertising items were stolen during this period. Nevertheless, the descriptions of the object and its movement given by the witnesses closely resembled those of a balloon.

summary: Observations by two witnesses of a large luminous phenomenon with red-orange and yellow colours in the night sky: observations of the Blood Moon.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named LA BAULE (44) 1979, is part of a group of recently re-examined cases. Two people (T1 and T2) observed, from their homes, a luminous phenomenon with a red-orange and yellow halo in the night sky above Pornichet. This very large phenomenon appeared stationary at first, then moved towards Saint-Nazaire; the halo gradually disappeared. No further witness statements were collected despite notices issued by the gendarmerie in the press and on the radio. The two witnesses most likely observed the Moon. The Moon (El 4.6e, Az 90.5) was indeed very low above Pornichet, as seen from the Penchateau headland. All descriptions point to a misinterpretation of the Moon rising on the horizon: - shapes: clouds were present that night; a partial and variable presence (a break) of clouds in front of the Moon could cause it to appear in all sorts of shapes. The mention of a halo also corresponds to the effect of the Moon's light being scattered by the mists and clouds near the break. T2 clearly distinguishes a fairly well-defined central shape (the opening) within a halo. T2 reports, "Indeed, I observed for about a minute a UFO, shaped like a demon, clearly standing out from a red halo"; - colors: depending on the thickness of the mist or cloud, the color can indeed vary from red to "violent yellow"; - size: the Moon with the surrounding halo can indeed correspond to the width of Pornichet seen from Pointe de Penchateau (3 or 5 degrees), as mentioned by T2. - perception of movement: this comes at the end of the observation, the UFO being described as stationary until then. T1 mentions a movement towards Saint-Nazaire. This is the classic illusion produced by the decrease in the angular size and/or brightness of a UFO (here, the gradual closing of the cloud gap on the Moon). The witness very logically interprets it as a movement away. The geography of the area perfectly allows for describing a movement beyond Pornichet, as seen from the Penchateau headland, as a movement towards Saint-Nazaire. T2, moreover, gives a very precise description of this apparent movement phenomenon: "When I saw this UFO moving, it moved gradually, at a fairly regular speed at first, then faster afterwards, but always with the same progression. It didn't disappear suddenly. I always saw this halo diminishing as the UFO moved away." Note T2's astonishment: "What struck me most is that this halo wasn't reflected either on the water or in the sky." T2 imagines the UFO (Unidentified Floating Object) to be at Pornichet, therefore just on the other side of the bay from the observation point. It's logical to look for a mirror effect (specular reflection) on the water at a point midway between the UFO and T2. But the Moon, like the clouds scattering its light, is much farther away. The reflection on the water cannot be specular but only due to a scattering effect, which is much less intense and depends on the surface roughness of the water (height and orientation of the wavelets), probably not strong enough that evening. Consequently, GEIPAN reclassifies the case as A: observation of the Blood Moon.

summary: Setting off fireworks without authorization.
description: On the night of July 18-19, 1979, several residents of the same neighborhood heard short, piercing noises between 9:30 p.m. and 12:15 a.m. These frightened individuals then saw unusual lights in the sky. This same phenomenon occurred again on the evening of July 20. The police investigation determined that these phenomena originated from whistling rockets launched playfully and without authorization from the garden of a neighboring house.

summary: Observing an object changing direction and speed
description: On July 16, 1979, at approximately 9:40 PM, two people observed a luminous object in the sky. This object was trapezoidal in shape, dark in color, with four lights at the front and a red light at the rear. Initially stationary above the Savoyard cove, the object moved slowly eastward. After a sudden acceleration, it rose vertically into the sky before disappearing. No sound was heard. No aircraft took off from or landed on the island after 8:00 PM, and no further reports were collected regarding this unexplained phenomenon.

summary: Recent testimony of an old observation. Observation of a stationary, rust-colored triangular object. Lack of precise information.
description: In 2011, a witness reported an old sighting. He did not recall the exact year and month (between 1979 and 1980, between mid-July and mid-August, and in the late afternoon). The date of the event was given arbitrarily. Observing the landscape with a telescope, the witness was intrigued by a stationary, triangular object, light rust-orange in color. The object was quickly obscured by mist and a cloud. The observation lasted less than 30 seconds. The object's triangular shape and slight movement suggested a torahedral balloon. Some weather balloons are brownish-orange, while the witness described it as rust-colored. However, the details of the object's surface described by the witness do not fit this hypothesis. As the precise date is unknown, it is not possible to verify wind conditions or balloon launches with Météo-France or CNES. Due to a lack of precise information, this case is classified as "C".

summary: observation of an unusual kite-like object
description: On July 14, 1979, between 9:50 and 9:55 PM, two witnesses observed a rounded object in the sky, shaped like a cauldron and stainless steel or aluminum in color, at an altitude of 100 to 150 meters. Its horizontal trajectory was northeast-southwest, and it moved with a regular, silent oscillating motion. Reflections appeared during its movement. No other reports of this phenomenon have been collected. Based on the description, and given that many unusual objects were seen moving at low altitudes on July 14th, these witnesses likely saw a kite.

summary: Observation of a luminous disk crossing the sky.
description: On July 14, 1979, at approximately 10:45 PM, a witness in the crowd watching the fireworks spotted a light in the sky (at 45°C) that intrigued him. He observed this luminosity for 8 to 12 seconds as it crossed the sky in a straight line from south to north at a constant speed. This object was shaped like a luminous disc with a small, less distinct tail. The witness noted variations in color, but no sound emanating from the object was perceptible. It disappeared quickly. Despite the crowd present at the time, no other accounts have been collected regarding this phenomenon, for which we lack information.

summary: Observations of silent evolutions in the mountainous landscape of the Esterel of a very bright spherical object: probable observation of a Mylar balloon.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case, previously classified as D and named SAINT-RAPHAEL (83) 1979, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined (see the investigation report). On July 13, 1979, at 1:10 PM, two witnesses (T1 and T2) working at the lookout post on Mont Vinaigre in the Esterel Massif, in the commune of Fréjus (83), were intrigued by the movements of a very bright, spherical object in the landscape. During their statements to the gendarmerie, a sketch was drawn showing the successive movements of this object (see the gendarmerie report). T2, using binoculars, described an object descending vertically from a cloud, moving down the hill in fits and starts, passing from one hill to another, stopping, and finally rising again and disappearing into a cloud. No other witness statements were collected. The radar services contacted by the gendarmerie detected nothing. The weather conditions at the time of observation are a key factor in understanding and explaining the complex movements of the UFO, which constituted the core of the case's strangeness. These conditions—namely, a maximum observed wind speed of 34 knots with turbulent airflow in the area—occurred in a region with rugged terrain. However, a minimum wind speed of only 10 to 15 knots is sufficient for a lighter-than-air balloon, such as a metallized nylon model (often called a Mylar balloon), to exhibit irregular horizontal and vertical movement. The inability (for any witness) to accurately perceive the distance of an unknown phenomenon can lead to overestimating distances and therefore speeds of movement based on angular displacements (the only ones truly perceived by the eyes), thus increasing the strangeness of the sight (a rapid jump from one hill to another, a sudden stop above the highway). These Mylar balloons can be inflated with air, but most often with helium, and can then fly for between two weeks and two months, carried by local winds. Such balloons have existed since the late 1970s and are often circular or oval in shape, sometimes decorated with a fanciful design. The visibility of this type of balloon is enhanced by their aluminized envelope, which strongly reflects sunlight; their shape is only truly discernible at a shorter distance. Furthermore, the strong reflection of sunlight, combined with the observation distance, makes it impossible to distinguish either the possible fanciful design or the inflation device. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of a Mylar balloon.

summary: observation of an object with a change in shape, color and trajectory.
description: On July 13, 1979, at approximately 11:30 PM, witnesses spotted an object in the sky that caught their attention. A reddish-orange sphere, about the size of a soccer ball, was moving at high altitude. During the observation, this object changed shape and color, then stopped before speeding off again and disappearing into the atmosphere. No further reports were collected about this phenomenon, which remains unexplained.

summary: Probable observation of a satellite.
description: On July 10th, around 3:00 AM, a witness observed a luminous mass moving diagonally from north to east through their window. Round or ovoid in shape and yellow in color, this object was visible for 10 to 15 minutes before disappearing. No sound was heard. This person likely observed the passage of a Transit or Oscar satellite, and not Skylab, which had not been visible in France since the end of June.

summary: Observation of a reddish-orange mass in the sky: astronomical observation of the Moon at sunset.
description: This observation was classified as a "C" case in 2008 by GEIPAN and was subsequently re-examined (see the document: Investigation Notes). On July 4, 1979, at 2:00 AM, a person returning home spotted a large, reddish-orange mass shaped like a shell. The frightened witness went inside and observed the phenomenon for two minutes; no sound was heard. The mass then disappeared into the landscape. No other witness accounts of this phenomenon were collected. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, color) with a well-known astronomical object: the Moon at sunset. Furthermore, the Moon was indeed visible in the observed area of the sky. The issue is not the witness's visual perception, but rather their interpretation of the observation based on their emotions (fatigue, fear). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of weak strangeness is classified as PAN A, an observation linked to a misinterpretation of the Moon.

summary: Observation of a bright flash and headaches.
description: Recent testimony (November 23, 2009) of an old sighting: In July 1979 (the witness does not remember the exact date), two people experienced severe headaches after observing a bright flash on a wall of their bedroom. These headaches disappeared at the same time as the light phenomenon. Looking out the window to determine the origin of this light, these two people observed several beams of light illuminating the road. The local newspaper later reported the presence of areas of scorched grass in a field in the area (no information is given regarding the name of the local newspaper or the date of publication of the article). No other testimonies have been collected regarding this old sighting, for which any investigation is difficult, if not impossible.

summary: Distant observations of a slow-moving red phenomenon: misinterpretation of the Moon at sunset.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. Among its publications are older cases, originally classified as type A to A, which are now being re-examined. The aim of this re-examination is not to lower or raise any particular classification category, but rather to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification within an investigation report. This particular case study is one of those classified as type A to A in 1979 by GEIPAN, under the name COULLONS (45) 10.06.1979. On June 30, 1979, at approximately 12:30 a.m., four people in a vehicle were traveling on the D 54 between Saint-Florent (45) and Villemurlin (45) (see the investigation report). Upon reaching the road near the hamlet of Pierrefitte, they spotted a red object in the distance that appeared to descend from the sky at road level. The shape described varied among witnesses (sometimes banana-shaped with points pointing upwards, sometimes teardrop-shaped). After stopping the car, they observed the UFO: no noise was heard, and no intermittent lights were observed on the UFO. The witnesses then saw the UFO move slowly. Frightened, they decided to turn around and head back towards Coullons to alert the police. One of the witnesses saw the UFO disappear behind the trees lining the road. Received by the gendarmes at 12:55 a.m., they immediately left for the indicated location without the witnesses. Initial observations that same night at 1:20 a.m. yielded no traces. The following day, the gendarmes, accompanied by the witnesses, returned to the presumed site of the UFO and discovered a fire with a diameter of 1.60 meters. The ashes were still hot. No other traces were found on the ground or in the vegetation, and no further witness statements were collected. The investigation revealed that two days prior (June 28), farmers had lit a brush fire. The gendarmes hypothesized that the witnesses had likely seen a whirlwind of embers from the brush fire, which would explain the pear or teardrop shape of the phenomenon as well as its red color. Despite a correlation between the apparent location of the UFO and the site of the brush fire, the hypothesis of mistaking the latter for the UFO is poorly suited to the UFO observation. Today, the plausible hypothesis of mistaking the moon is supported not only by the fact that the moon was setting, which is perfectly consistent with the red color of the UFO, but also by the fact that its azimuth (281°) perfectly matches that of the axis of the D54 road. Furthermore, the visual appearance of the moon at sunset is perfectly consistent with that of the UFO as described by witnesses, with the crescent moon positioned on the horizon. Although the witnesses do not mention the presence of the moon, it was visible along the axis they indicate. The perfect consistency between the moon's true position, its location, and the descriptions provided by the witnesses leaves no doubt about the misinterpretation. It is not the witnesses' visual perception that is at issue, but their interpretation of their observations based on their feelings (fatigue, driving, fear). GEIPAN classifies this case as A: mistaking the moon for moonset.

summary: Probable sighting of an aircraft passing overhead.
description: On June 30, 1979, at approximately 11:30 PM, motorists were driving on a departmental road when they spotted a bright light in the sky. A point of light, initially stationary, gradually moved closer to the witnesses. Two lights, one red and one green, on either side of the point, flashed alternately. A whooshing sound was heard as it passed over the frightened witnesses, and a triangular shape was seen. The object moved rapidly southward. This information corresponds to nighttime descriptions of aircraft flights (noise, geometry, and light colors). These witnesses likely observed an airplane.

summary: observation of atmospheric reentry.
description: On June 21, 1979, at 10:25 PM local time, several sailors aboard a French Navy vessel in the Ionian Sea (latitude 38°02'N and longitude 17°41'E) observed a luminous phenomenon 15 arcseconds above the horizon. A bright point of light suddenly split into three luminous parts, the intensity of which gradually decreased. The colors changed from white to orange and then back to white. The observed trajectory was southwest-east. The high-speed phenomenon was observed for one minute. These individuals likely witnessed an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of flashes on the horizon due to military firing.
description: On June 15, 1979, around 11:00 PM, several people observed an intriguing orange glow on the horizon. This glow, located in the Northwest, appeared to be composed of several points of light. The observation lasted about ten minutes before disappearing. That same evening, a surface-to-air missile firing exercise took place at the nearby military camp, located northwest of the witnesses' position, between 11:00 PM and 11:30 PM. These individuals witnessed the glows associated with the firing.

summary: Observation above the horizon of the slow movement of a luminous phenomenon followed by another blinking luminous phenomenon with an upward trajectory: lack of information.
description: On June 10, 1979, between 3:30 and 4:00 AM, after a thunderstorm, a witness observed a mysterious luminous phenomenon through a window. He saw a powerful light in the southwest, above the horizon. It moved slowly horizontally, occasionally making vertical movements. Depending on the light's position, the witness saw luminous circles. A second, flashing light, coming from the north, appeared and passed over the first. It quickly disappeared in the south. At 4:00 AM, the light was still present, so the witness went to bed. No noise was heard, and no other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of a red ball with smoke
description: On Friday, June 8, 1979, between 1:00 PM and 1:05 PM, several people witnessed a peculiar phenomenon over the bay. They first observed a vertical plume of smoke that gradually dissipated. A few minutes later, a spherical, bright red object crossed the sky in a straight line toward the southwest, curving downwards. Moving rather slowly, this object was followed by a white or grayish plume of smoke. The observations lasted only a few seconds, during which no sound was heard. An investigation by the gendarmerie, in consultation with the navy, revealed that tests of distress and flares had been conducted. However, the information provided was too imprecise to confirm this hypothesis.

summary: Observation of a luminous ball following the witness.
description: On June 3, 1979, at approximately 11:30 PM, a driver observed an orange sphere of light in her rearview mirror. It appeared to follow her to a nearby town, where, frightened, she honked her horn to warn the residents. One person came out of their house but refused to investigate. Continuing her journey, she saw the object all the way home. The witness experienced physical sensations, and the dashboard went dark. The object made no noise and was located at a low altitude in the north-northwest. She encountered no other vehicles, and no further reports of this phenomenon were collected. Despite the lack of information, the night sky chart indicated the presence of Jupiter, particularly visible (magnitude -1.47), Pollux (magnitude 0.98), and Capella. The hypothesis of an astronomical observation is probable but cannot be confirmed. The witness experienced a significant fright, which likely explains his behavior and the effects he felt.

summary: Observation of a slowly moving triangular-shaped object
description: On June 3, 1979, at 5:45 PM, a witness observed a strange object moving from north to south across the sky for 7 to 8 minutes. This triangular object was red in color. The witness observed no noise or trail. No other accounts have been collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observing a moonset with a conjunction of planets.
description: On May 31, 1979, at 12:40 AM, two people observed a luminous phenomenon in the western sky. For several minutes, a large, crescent-shaped, orange object was visible. Another object also appeared briefly. The star chart that morning indicated the presence of Jupiter (magnitude -1.49), Pollux (magnitude 0.98), and a setting moon (magnitude -9.51) in the western sky. These individuals made an astronomical observation of this constellation.

summary: Observation of a flat object emitting a bright orange trail.
description: On May 30, 1979, two people observed a peculiar phenomenon in the sky for 20 minutes. An object shaped like a flattened rugby ball crossed the sky from southeast to northwest. The witnesses noticed a bright orange trail of varying length following the object, which was located at an altitude of approximately 500 meters. One of the witnesses, a student pilot, did not recognize it as an aircraft. No other accounts of this phenomenon have been collected, and information such as the time of observation is lacking.

summary: Moon observation.
description: On May 29, 1979, at approximately 11:30 PM, a motorist driving on a small country road was surprised to see a bright orange crescent-shaped object approaching him. This low-altitude object appeared to follow the motorist as he traveled northwest. No sound was heard. The object was then lost from sight. The following day, the witness returned to the same location and observed the same object, but this time white. It disappeared behind the woods, heading northwest. The night sky chart indicates the presence of the Moon at a low altitude to the northwest, with a magnitude of -8.91: this person made an astronomical observation of the Moon. The impression of lunar movement as one travels is well known.

summary: unidentified radar echoes
description: On May 26, 1979, at 2:30 a.m. local time, two witnesses on watch aboard a cargo ship observed for two to three minutes a group of four juxtaposed radar echoes forming a large echo with sharp edges, as seen on a V22 radar. The nature of the echo was not consistent with weather jamming or multiple hull reflections. The vessel was sailing in the Pacific Ocean north of Chimborazo, a volcano in Ecuador.

summary: Probable observation of an aircraft on approach.
description: On May 25, 1979, at 1:10 a.m., two on-duty police officers observed a moving and intriguing luminous phenomenon in the sky. At low altitude, four oval-shaped, yellowish-white lights gradually passed overhead before changing direction. They were unable to determine whether the lights belonged to a single object or were separate phenomena. A faint humming sound was heard before the phenomenon disappeared to the southeast, hidden by the landscape. No interference was detected on their onboard equipment. The description given by the witnesses and the proximity of several airfields (in addition to Lyon-Satolas) strongly suggest that the two officers witnessed an aircraft on approach.

summary: Observation of a metallic-colored object moving approximately 20 meters above the ground.
description: On May 15, 1979, between 2:15 and 2:45 PM, several people in a field spotted an object on the ground that then slowly rose horizontally. Spherical in shape and metallic in color, it moved by oscillating, following the contours of the terrain, and gained speed as it moved vertically. Some witnesses were able to see it for about 30 minutes before it gradually disappeared. No information was gathered about a possible weather balloon launch in the area, but based on the descriptions given, these people likely saw a balloon.

summary: Observation of a silvery object descending slowly and then rising vertically again
description: On May 14, 1979, at approximately 1:00 PM, several people observed a bright object in the clear, windless sky. The object was oval-shaped and silvery in color; it moved slowly, oscillating along a north-south trajectory and gradually losing altitude. Appearing to fall behind a hill, one of the witnesses went to investigate and saw the object rise rapidly before disappearing. The witnesses heard no noise. While this hypothesis has not been definitively proven, it is likely that they saw a balloon.

summary: Observing a moonset.
description: On May 8, 1979, at 4:40 a.m., a motorist noticed a luminous phenomenon that intrigued her. A reddish-orange sphere with corkscrew-shaped antennae moved and quickly disappeared to the southwest. The gendarmes' analysis indicated that it could not have been the moon, given that a check carried out the following day at the same time showed that the moon was further to the left of the vehicle than the witness observed. In fact, a precise analysis of the sky showed that on May 8, at the time of the observation, the moon was indeed aligned with the observation and had disappeared by the time of the observation. It is therefore evident that the witness observed a rather bright moonset. The presence of clouds likely caused reflections or glare, and the rapid disappearance reported by the witness is easily explained by the fact that she herself was driving. The verification carried out on May 9 at the same time is not conclusive since the moon is then further west and higher on the horizon, which allows it to be recognized without ambiguity.

summary: Observation of the passage of a large vehicle.
description: On April 27, 1979, at approximately 11:30 PM, a witness observed a gigantic orange craft moving from west to east for 30 seconds. It disappeared abruptly without leaving a trail. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observations of three lights in the sky and a circular object.
description: On several evenings in April 1979, between 11:00 PM and midnight, two people observed three flashing white and red lights arranged in a triangle in the sky. On April 17, between 11:00 PM and 11:30 PM, while walking home along a country road, these people saw one of these lights move rapidly towards the ground: it appeared to come from a flattened, circular object approximately two meters in diameter. Despite observing it for several minutes, the witnesses could not determine whether the object, then 200 meters away, was resting on the ground or hovering above it, as it emitted a very intense light. Frightened, they returned home with stinging eyes. The police found no trace of it on the ground or in the surrounding area. No other witness statements were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of a bright point
description: On Sunday, April 15, 1979, at approximately 10:45 PM, witnesses observed a moving point of light in the sky. Upon stopping, it changed color while twinkling. Police officers called to the scene found a point of light the size of a star moving slowly eastward. Information regarding the direction and altitude of the observation is lacking, but it was likely an astronomical observation, perhaps of Vega.

summary: Observation of a large dark mass projecting an intense light.
description: On April 7, 1979, at approximately 6:15 a.m., a driver and his passenger were surprised to see a very intense white fluorescent light in a field; it illuminated the ground for several meters. The light appeared to come from a dark, rounded mass larger than a car. This observation lasted only a few seconds before the light completely disappeared. The field, located on a ridge, is bordered by a public road. No traces of the object were found on the ground. No further accounts of this phenomenon were collected, and information about it remains scarce.

summary: Observation of bright flashes at high altitude: observation of an aircraft during a training flight.
description: On April 2, 1979, at approximately 8:40 PM, the gendarmerie received telephone calls reporting an object emitting a bright light flying over the town. Upon arrival, the gendarmes observed an orange luminous phenomenon moving across the clear sky at low altitude towards the northeast. Flashing red lights and a steady green light emanated from the object. The investigation determined that it was a DC-9 aircraft conducting flight training in the area between 8:30 PM and 9:15 PM. The case is classified as Class A: observation of an aircraft.

summary: Observation of a block of ice falling near a train station.
description: On March 31, 1979, the gendarmerie was contacted regarding a piece of ice that had fallen onto the train station parking lot. There were no injuries or damage, despite ice fragments scattered over approximately thirty meters. Beige and red substances were found in one of the ice fragments. Samples of this material were analyzed, concluding that it contained vegetable or animal fat originating from a block of ice that had likely broken off from an aircraft. The village is indeed located under a busy flight path, and specific weather conditions can cause such incidents.

summary: Observation of a ball making back-and-forth movements
description: On March 22nd, around 11 PM, a witness observed an orange sphere, about the size of a soccer ball, at high altitude. It moved horizontally, making a rapid back-and-forth motion; then it moved vertically, emitting green reflections. The same phenomenon occurred the following day at the same location and time. No other reports were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of an object shaped like a "slice" of orange, luminous, with the sound of an airplane.
description: On March 22, 1979, at approximately 9:25 PM, a driver and his passenger spotted a dazzling light. For two to three minutes, these witnesses observed, at a distance of 100 meters, an object shaped like an orange slice with a flashing light on its left side and a row of spotlights of different colors. This object then moved rapidly toward the southwest. A distant humming sound was heard. Photographs were taken by one of the witnesses but were never submitted to the police. No further information was gathered about this phenomenon, for which we lack details.

summary: Observation of a luminous object that appears to follow a motorist for 10 kilometers: astronomical observation of the Moon.
description: On March 21, 1979, around 2:00 AM, a motorist driving on the D16 between Ayguesvives and Gardouch (31) spotted a luminous phenomenon that took on varying shapes and colors throughout the journey and seemed to follow the witness. During the 10 kilometers traveled, the UFO sometimes appeared to stop and then accelerate significantly. Upon arriving home, the witness woke his wife, who also observed the phenomenon. The witness took photos before going to bed around 3:00 AM. No unusual noises were heard, and no other statements were collected by the gendarmerie. The GEPAN investigation concluded that the witness had likely made an astronomical observation of a moonrise in foggy weather (see the GEPAN investigation report). A check carried out in 2008 on the astronomical configuration at the time of the observation also shows a conjunction between the Moon, Neptune and Antares, which confirms the conclusion of the GEPAN survey of 1979. This case is class A: astronomical observation of the Moon.

summary: Observation of a luminous sphere. Orange weather.
description: On March 19, 1979, between 11:10 PM and 11:15 PM, two witnesses observed a mysterious luminous phenomenon from their villa.
