Looking out of a window, they saw a large, bluish-white sphere hovering about fifty meters above the ground. This phenomenon was observed for about thirty seconds before gradually fading away. That same night, a violent orange storm struck Nice, and lightning flashed across the sky. The witness went to the site on March 21 and learned that lightning had struck a pylon on March 19 around 11:10 PM, creating a huge ball of light. This person likely witnessed an electrical phenomenon related to the storm.

summary: Observation of a rocket-shaped object
description: On March 18, 1979, at approximately 9:15 PM, a driver and her passenger spotted a dark, fluorescent gray, rocket-shaped object three meters above the highway. This silent object moved slowly northward. The car quickly passed beneath it. On the return trip, around 9:45 PM, the same driver saw, in roughly the same spot, a flat wing measuring three square meters above the highway. She described the object as being made of a gray metal mesh a few centimeters thick, and appearing to have a wavy motion. The object, flying over the car, stopped three or four meters in front of her vehicle. Impressed, the driver accelerated to quickly pass beneath the object without hearing any unusual noise or seeing any lights. No heat source appeared to emanate from the object. These observations lasted only a few seconds, occurring in poor weather conditions (continuous rain overnight) and near Brest-Guipavas airport. No trace of the event was found by the police, and no further information was gathered regarding this phenomenon, which remains unidentified.

summary: Observation of two objects moving at very high speed.
description: On March 18, 1979, at approximately 9:45 PM, a witness observed a mysterious luminous phenomenon from his yard for about five seconds. He saw two orange spheres, each about 15 cm in diameter, appear and disappear within the clouds at arm's length. The spheres moved at high speed from west to southeast. They were about 50 cm apart. No sound was heard. Despite an appeal for witnesses issued by the gendarmerie, no further information was collected about this phenomenon, for which we lack details.

summary: Observation of an orange glow crossing the sky
description: On March 15, 1979, at approximately 7:25 a.m., five people working on railway track repairs spotted a luminous phenomenon that intrigued them. An orange glow, about the size of a football, slowly crossed the sky from east to west on a downward trajectory. The observation, which lasted about 30 seconds, revealed a trail of white smoke. No sound was heard. The object disappeared, hidden by the landscape. These people likely witnessed an atmospheric reentry, which, given the limited observation time, could have been space debris.

summary: Observations of a powerful luminous phenomenon and power outage: observations and consequences on animals of an electric arc on the EDF power line
description: On the night of March 11, 1979, around 12:45 a.m., several people witnessed a peculiar luminous phenomenon. They were dazzled by a very bright blue-green-purple light that illuminated the surrounding landscape for about a minute. A power outage affected the entire town. A motorist reported that he and his wife saw a slightly oval, motionless mass 15 to 20 meters above the ground. This mass suddenly went out, revealing a red-orange fire on either side. A fish farmer, awakened on the night of March 11 by a crackling noise and an intense light, discovered on Tuesday, March 13, that numerous fish had died in one of his fish farms (1800 kg in total). A 10,000-volt power line runs above the pond, and during the night of March 14-15, one of the wires snapped: it was damaged over a length of 4 to 5 meters. The EDF (French electricity company) representative for the area was unable to report the incident on the control line, as the power outage in the town was too brief (1 minute). These individuals witnessed an electrical arc on the EDF line, which likely contributed to the fish deaths, although tests revealed a viral infection. We have no information on the precise nature of this infection or its potential impact on fish mortality.

summary: probable aircraft sighting
description: Between 9:30 p.m. and 10:30 p.m. on March 26, 1979, motorists spotted an object in the sky illuminated by three lights. One light was white, and the other two were flashing green and red. This object moved rapidly, changing direction. One of the witnesses indicated that he had made this observation several times between February and March. These people likely observed a helicopter-type aircraft.

summary: observation of a round shape changing color.
description: On February 14, 1979, at 9:00 PM, a witness observed a round, white shape in the sky that changed color while moving rapidly along a south-southeast trajectory. No other reports were collected about this phenomenon, for which we lack data.

summary: Observation of a stationary and luminous object.
description: On February 6, 1979, at 9:20 a.m., a passerby observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky that intrigued him. For two minutes, he saw a saucer-shaped object with blue and yellow lines at the rear, which then disappeared. The object was subsequently hidden by buildings, and when the witness rediscovered it, he noticed a denser, rounded light at its center. The object was stationary within a luminous halo and formed a 20° angle with the ground. No other reports were collected. At that time, the sun was very low on the horizon and directly in line with the observation: it was probably a reflection of the sun through the clouds.

summary: Observation of an orange, hemispherical object: misinterpretation of the moon at sunset.
description: On February 4, 1979, at approximately 1:15 a.m., a witness observed a luminous object in the sky from their vehicle for 30 seconds. This object was shaped like an orange hemisphere and moved from southwest to northeast along a horizontal trajectory. The object gradually disappeared and diminished in size. This observation was initially published by GEIPAN (the French National Center for Experimental Observations on Astronomy) as a Category C report due to a lack of information. An internet user, passionate about astronomy, identified this case as a possible case of mistaken identity with the setting moon; to verify this hypothesis, they returned to the observation site in February 2015, 36 years after the event. The Earth's and Moon's orbits are such that the period during which the Earth and Moon are in the same relative positions with respect to the Sun corresponds to 223 lunar months, or 6,585.32 days: this period is called the Saros period; it is used to calculate the interval between lunar and solar eclipses. It should be noted that, after this period, which is not a whole number of days, solar time is therefore not the same. In our case, between the date of observation and the day of reconstruction, it was necessary to count this period of nearly 18 years twice: the exact date falls on February 25, 2015, at 4:36 PM, therefore at a local time significantly different from the time of observation. To choose the best reconstruction date, it is necessary to find, close to that date, the moments when the Moon's azimuth and angular height (elevation) are closest to those of the observation. Two dates prove suitable: - February 23, 2015 at 11:55 PM, with a Moon at an angular height of 1.1 arcseconds and an azimuth of 288 arcseconds, a 5-day lunar month, and a phase two days before the First Quarter. - February 25, 2015 at 1:00 AM (therefore the night of February 24-25), with a Moon at an angular height of 1.5 arcseconds and an azimuth of 292 arcseconds, a 6-day lunar month, and a phase on the eve of the First Quarter. For comparison, the Moon's position during the observation at Boulay-sur-Moselle was 1.4 arcseconds in angular height and an azimuth of 286 arcseconds (the reconstruction was therefore done with a lunar position perfectly similar to that of 1979), with a lunar month of 6.7 days and a First Quarter phase. GEIPAN publishes the complete observation report of this amateur astronomer, a very well-documented report whose conclusion is as follows: The testimony from that time corresponds in many respects to the observation made during the reconstruction: the shape is indeed a hemisphere of orange color tending towards red, and its inclination is indeed almost horizontal. The duration of the observation could indeed have been brief, as the Moon was low and located close to the horizon. Furthermore, the presence of clouds that could have obscured it at any time can be assumed. The observation site, shown on the map attached to the police report, presents a topographical peculiarity that could have surprised the witness. Indeed, this location has a significant change in elevation, where one passes from a point at an altitude of 324m to a point at an altitude of 340m over an almost straight distance of barely 250m. The slope is therefore approximately 6%. This configuration of the terrain can, for example, when driving a motor vehicle, give the illusion of objects on the horizon suddenly appearing, objects that were previously hidden by the sky. These various elements thus support the hypothesis of confusion due to the Moon being seen under particular conditions (unusual appearance of the Moon at sunset, impression of sudden appearance at the top of the sky). This entirely convincing reconstruction allows us to classify this case as A: observation of the Moon at sunset.

summary: Observation of 2 light sources.
description: On December 31, 1979 (not January as indicated in the report under the heading "Investigation"), between 11:15 PM and 12:30 AM, two witnesses observed two unusual lights in the sky. These lights sometimes appeared to be connected by a series of very bright, multicolored, serpentine lines. The observation was not continuous, and the phenomenon disappeared completely around 1:00 AM. No further reports were collected regarding this phenomenon, for which we lack sufficient data.

summary: Observation of a bright point at high altitude, with changing direction and variable speed.
description: On January 29, 1979, between 8:30 and 8:45 PM, a witness observed a bright orange point of light following a flash of lightning. Initially stationary, this point began a slow descent towards the ground while growing larger. It then changed direction, moving horizontally at very high speed and disappearing. No sound was heard during the observation, which lasted approximately two to three minutes. A hypothesis put forward by the Florac Observatory, contacted by the gendarmerie regarding this observation, was that of a "ball lightning" phenomenon, but we lack sufficient data to confirm or refute this hypothesis.

summary: Observation of a luminous sphere. No noise.
description: On January 26, 1979, at 12:45 a.m., a motorist spotted a luminous sphere about 150 meters ahead, close to the ground. As he approached, he saw that this sphere, 4 to 5 meters in diameter, was made up of several panels. Antennas measuring 1 to 2 meters were visible, as well as small blue and white flames. No sound was heard. The sphere disappeared as it moved toward the horizon. No further information has been gathered about this phenomenon, for which we lack data.

summary: Observations of a triangular-shaped object, slow progression and whistling sound.
description: witness made two separate observations on two different dates: Around 10:00 PM on January 25, 1979, this witness, accompanied by another person, noticed that their vehicle was illuminated by a headlight above it. Taking the time to stop, they saw a triangular-shaped object emitting lights of different colors, but predominantly reddish-orange. These lights were accompanied by two spotlights that were turned on and pointed towards the ground. The object moved slowly, emitting a whistling sound. Although located very close to the witness (5 meters), the witness was unable to assess the size of the object, which then disappeared behind a hill. The second observation took place around 8:00 PM on February 10, 1979: From their apartment, the witness reported hearing a humming sound coming from outside. He then observed an object composed of two parts, emitting white and red lights and moving in a north-south direction. Upon reaching the area above the town, the object was joined by a series of bright, moving objects, also emitting lights, for half an hour. Despite the significant duration of this luminous phenomenon, no further accounts were collected regarding it, for which we lack information.

summary: observation of an aircraft
description: On January 19, 1979, at approximately 6:30 PM, two motorists noticed two bright white lights in the sky, as well as a red and orange glow emanating from an unidentified object. They observed movement toward the southeast, but no noise was heard. No other witnesses were able to provide information. During the investigation, it was established that training flights by a twin-engine aircraft had taken place on January 19 between 5:30 PM and 7:00 PM. This aircraft was equipped with two powerful searchlights at the front, and the aircraft had performed U-turns over the area in question.

summary: Observation of a bright sphere moving slowly: probable astronomical observation of Venus.
description: This observation case was classified as C in 2008 by GEIPAN (the French UFO investigation group). It was the subject of a new investigation (see the document: Investigation Notes). On January 14, 1979, between 5:30 and 7:00 AM, two witnesses observed a luminous phenomenon in the eastern sky that intrigued them. A bright sphere, larger than the stars, moved silently and slowly in an east-south direction. The primary witness did not provide details regarding the sphere's altitude. No other witness statements were collected about this phenomenon. This case is consistent, but the description of the observed UFO is rather vague in the police report. The witness's sincerity and credibility have never been questioned. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, color) with a well-known astronomical object: Venus, which was clearly visible in the observed area of the sky. In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of weak strangeness is classified as PAN B, probable observation of the planet Venus, through a light layer of haze or by a halo effect.

summary: observation of a luminous phenomenon composed of two spheres.
description: On January 13, 1979, at 6:15 a.m., a witness observed a curious luminous phenomenon in the courtyard of their home. An object shaped like a dumbbell was stationary in the sky. Two pale yellow spheres, surrounded by a halo, were connected by a bright blue-violet section. After a few seconds of observation, the object moved off at high speed and disappeared, hidden behind the rooftops. No other witnesses to this phenomenon were found that day. On January 14, another person witnessed a different luminous phenomenon. We lack information about these events.

summary: probable astronomical observation
description: On January 13, 1979, starting at 8:00 PM, several witnesses observed a luminous object in the sky, displaying different colors and emitting reflections. The observation lasted about thirty minutes. The object was located to the right of the Moon, but the distance between the Moon and the observation point was unknown. The witnesses likely made an astronomical observation, which could have been either Procyon (magnitude 0.40), particularly visible at this time of year, or Sirius, whose reflections of different colors are well known and, in this case, accentuated by observation with binoculars. Jupiter is also particularly visible, but to the left of the Moon, which does not correspond to the witness's account. These witnesses were absent for three hours, and upon their return around midnight, they saw the same luminous phenomenon, but farther away and having moved southward, which corresponds to the natural movement of the stars.

summary: probable observation of Venus
description: On January 13, 1979, between 6:15 and 8:30 a.m., a witness observed a bright point of light from his home, which intrigued him. This point moved slowly from east to west in an upward trajectory. The witness took several photographs. The descriptions provided and the star chart for that day indicate that this witness made an astronomical observation of Venus, which was particularly visible at that time of year (magnitude -4.41).

summary: observation of an airliner
description: On January 11, 1979, at approximately 6:45 a.m., a witness spotted an intriguing object from a window. Above a road, an oval object was moving silently. This object had six fixed red and green lights on its underside. In the center, a bright yellow light emitted a significant beam. The object was moving from east to west at a slow speed. According to the investigation, the witness saw a twin-engine FBOOM airliner that landed at 6:42 a.m. and took off again at 6:59 a.m. from the nearby Brive airfield.

summary: Probable observation of fragments of gondola or weather balloon envelope.
description: On January 11, 1979, at 4:35 PM, two witnesses spotted about fifteen flying objects in the sky. They appeared to be between 60 and 80 cm in diameter. Metallic in color, they swirled and emitted flashes of light as they reflected the setting sun. They moved slowly and silently toward the southeast, where they disappeared. A weather balloon launch took place the same day at noon, and it is likely that the witnesses saw fragments of the balloon's gondola or envelope.

summary: probable sighting of a helicopter
description: On January 6, 1979, around 10:00 PM, a person was walking their dog around their property. Suddenly, the dog, very frightened, began to growl and took refuge under a tree. The witness then spotted a very bright, motionless shape about 15 meters above the ground. A circular object topped with a dome emitted blinding lights and a faint hissing sound. The witness observed the object for two minutes from a building. After a swaying motion, the object disappeared at very high speed to the west at 10:04 PM. No other witness statements were collected, and no traces were observed on the ground the following day. Based on the noise and the observed swaying motion, the witness likely saw a helicopter.

summary: observations of objects in the sky
description: On January 3, 1979, at 6:50 a.m., two people observed a bright, low-altitude object in a south-southeast direction. Semi-spherical and accompanied by a shower of sparks, this object moved gradually and silently before disappearing to the south. These individuals were likely making an astronomical observation of Venus, which was particularly visible in the sky at that time (magnitude 4.46), according to the star chart. Around 7:00 p.m. that same day, a motorist driving by saw another flying object. For three to four seconds, he saw a sphere moving silently at a very high altitude on a north-south trajectory. This person likely saw a weather balloon, but we lack information about this latter object.

summary: observation of a luminous object above a built-up area.
description: On the night of January 1st to 2nd, 1979, two witnesses observed an object illuminated by red lights for less than 10 seconds. This object, which they likened to a kite, moved rapidly from north to south without any noise and at an altitude of approximately 100 meters above the town. No other witnesses were found regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: prolonged observation of a bright ball
description: On January 12, 1979, at approximately 7:30 PM, a person observed a peculiar luminous phenomenon in the north-northeast sky. For 20 minutes, the witness, using binoculars, observed an orange fireball about the size of a fist. No sound was heard. The phenomenon disappeared into the clouds. No other accounts have been collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Sighting of a cigar-shaped object and flashes of light.
description: Between January 24 and 28, 1979, three witnesses observed unusual phenomena in the same area. On January 24, between 7:00 and 7:15 a.m., a witness reported seeing an orange, cigar-shaped object. It moved slowly along a north-south trajectory and suddenly rose vertically before disappearing at high speed, changing color. No naval air force maneuvers were reported during this period, and no other reports were collected about this phenomenon, for which we lack information. On January 28, around 10:15 p.m., two other people saw luminous phenomena. Blue and white lights with a red dot (according to one witness) appeared at regular intervals. According to the gendarmerie investigation, these lights came from the navigation lights located on the keels of a German cargo ship anchored in a bay. This separate observation is classified as Category A.

summary: Observation of a small luminous ball. No noise.
description: On March 25, 1979, between 9:55 p.m. and 10:10 p.m., a witness observed a curious luminous phenomenon in the sky from his observation post at the factory. He first saw a milky white, arc-shaped light followed by a green sphere with a red dot in the center, which moved in various ways. No sound was heard. This witness and two other firefighters had already observed a similar luminous phenomenon earlier that year. No other accounts of the March 25th phenomenon have been collected, and we lack further information about it.
